note: The pathways Library compounds act through, from each member's own fact sheet (what it is). Sig's Relatives agent uses them: a compound that raises a hormone the body makes stands a rung below that hormone's own evidence, so the hormone's findings are said as expected from how the compound works, not tested; members that act on the same receptor are relatives too. The Combination agent uses them to say whether compounds taken together work through the same receptor (overlap), the same hormone by different routes, or different pathways. Nothing here is a finding. Compounds that change a hormone in other ways (aromatase inhibitors, other SERMs, GnRH drugs given continuously) are left out on purpose: their other effects mean the hormone's findings don't carry over.
